decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for recorded event types?
cards.back: The RMV driving record tracks civil motor-vehicle infractions, criminal violations and crashes with more than fifty percent fault.

cards.front: What is the rule for loss of driving privileges?
cards.back: A suspension or revocation removes driving privileges for a fixed period or indefinitely.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for nonrenewal obligations?
cards.back: An expired license cannot be renewed while listed unpaid parking, excise-tax or toll obligations or outstanding court warrants remain.

cards.front: What is the rule for citation consequences?
cards.back: A motor-vehicle citation may lead to a fine, loss of driving privileges, a court appearance or imprisonment.

cards.front: What is the rule for criminal examples?
cards.back: Driving under the influence and leaving a crash scene are examples of criminal motor-vehicle offenses.

cards.front: What is the rule for repeated violations?
cards.back: Repeated violations such as speeding or disobeying traffic signals can cause loss of a license.

cards.front: What is the rule for higher penalty conditions?
cards.back: Junior status, age below twenty-one and repeat offenses can increase penalties for many violations.

cards.front: What is the rule for multiple penalties?
cards.back: A single motor-vehicle offense can carry multiple penalties, including a fine, license loss and imprisonment.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for civil infraction?
cards.back: A civil motor-vehicle infraction is noncriminal and can usually be resolved by paying its fine.

cards.front: What is the rule for civil response deadline?
cards.back: A driver receiving a civil citation has twenty days to pay or request a hearing to contest it.

cards.front: What is the rule for civil safety surcharge?
cards.back: Civil fines under Massachusetts General Laws chapters eighty-nine or ninety receive an additional five-dollar public-safety surcharge.

cards.front: What is the rule for civil hearing fee?
cards.back: Requesting a civil-citation hearing requires a twenty-five-dollar RMV filing fee.

cards.front: What is the rule for complete exoneration refund?
cards.back: The hearing filing fee is refunded when the court finds the driver not responsible for every violation on the civil citation.

cards.front: What is the rule for late civil response?
cards.back: Failure to respond to a civil citation within twenty days results in responsibility and a substantial late fee.

cards.front: What is the rule for unpaid civil citation?
cards.back: Failure to pay a civil citation and its late fee causes license suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for recorded responsibility?
cards.back: Paying a civil fine accepts responsibility, and responsibility also appears on the record after a court orders payment or the driver fails to respond within twenty days.

cards.front: What is the rule for moving violation record?
cards.back: The RMV records Massachusetts moving violations, which can increase insurance rates and lead to license suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for parking ticket administration?
cards.back: Parking violations are handled by the issuing municipality rather than as civil motor-vehicle infractions.

cards.front: What is the rule for unpaid parking consequence?
cards.back: Unpaid parking violations block renewal of the driver license or vehicle registration.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for minimum speeding amount?
cards.back: The minimum speeding penalty is a one-hundred-dollar fine plus a five-dollar public-safety surcharge.

cards.front: What is the rule for additional speeding amount?
cards.back: For speed more than ten miles per hour above the limit, an extra ten dollars is charged for each mile per hour beyond that first ten.

cards.front: What is the rule for source speeding example?
cards.back: The manual illustrates a total fine of one hundred eighty-five dollars for seventy-three miles per hour in a fifty-five-mile-per-hour zone.

cards.front: What is the rule for included head injury surcharge?
cards.back: Every speeding fine includes a fifty-dollar surcharge directed to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund.

cards.front: What is the rule for work zone speeding?
cards.back: Speeding in a posted work zone doubles the speeding fine.

cards.front: What is the rule for repeated speeding suspension?
cards.back: Three speeding findings within twelve months cause a thirty-day license suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for junior speeding penalties?
cards.back: A Junior Operator’s first speeding offense causes a ninety-day suspension, and later offenses cause a one-year suspension.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for criminal immediate consequences?
cards.back: A criminal motor-vehicle offense can result in immediate arrest, towing, license seizure and detention until court.

cards.front: What is the rule for court criminal penalty?
cards.back: After conviction of a criminal motor-vehicle offense, the court sets the fine or prison sentence.

cards.front: What is the rule for criminal driving offenses?
cards.back: Driving with a suspended license, driving under the influence and leaving a crash scene are criminal motor-vehicle offenses.

cards.front: What is the rule for identify driver and owner?
cards.back: Refusing to give an officer the driver’s or vehicle owner’s name and address may lead to arrest and criminal charges.

cards.front: What is the rule for show documents and sign?
cards.back: Refusing to show the driver license or valid vehicle registration, or to sign in front of the officer, may lead to arrest and criminal charges.

cards.front: What is the rule for interstate record effect?
cards.back: Out-of-state motor-vehicle violations affect the Massachusetts driving record as though committed in Massachusetts.

cards.front: What is the rule for resolve outside obligations?
cards.back: Failure to pay or appear for an out-of-state violation affects Massachusetts license status and operating privileges.

cards.front: What is the rule for Massachusetts interstate penalty?
cards.back: Massachusetts applies its own suspension penalties to out-of-state violations, and its penalty can be stricter than the other state’s.

cards.front: What is the rule for interstate reinstatement?
cards.back: Reinstatement after an out-of-state obligation suspension requires proof of resolution and a Massachusetts reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for insurer fault standard?
cards.back: The at-fault crash test includes an insurer finding under a listed fault standard, such as driving on the wrong side or striking a vehicle from behind.

cards.front: What is the rule for insurer payment condition?
cards.back: The additional insurer-payment condition is more than one thousand dollars for collision, limited collision or another person’s property damage, or more than one thousand dollars for bodily injury when the same incident lacks collision or property damage above that amount.

cards.front: What is the rule for fault crash record?
cards.back: Charged at-fault crashes are entered on the driving record and count with violations toward possible suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for surchargeable event?
cards.back: Motor-vehicle violations and at-fault crashes are surchargeable events that count toward possible suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for speeding window start?
cards.back: The twelve-month window for three speeding violations begins when the driver pays or is found guilty of the first citation.

cards.front: What is the rule for junior racing penalties?
cards.back: A first Junior Operator drag-racing citation causes a one-year suspension, while a later citation causes a three-year suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for three event retraining?
cards.back: Three surchargeable events in two years require driver retraining, which must be completed within ninety days to avoid suspension until completion.

cards.front: What is the rule for seven event suspension?
cards.back: Seven surchargeable events within three years cause an automatic sixty-day suspension.

cards.front: What is the rule for insurance record rating?
cards.back: The Merit Rating Board administers the Safe Driver Insurance Plan, which uses driving records to determine insurance premiums.

cards.front: What is the rule for record and insurance cost?
cards.back: Moving-violation convictions or crash fault above fifty percent increase the insurance rate under the described plan, while safe driving may reduce it.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for retraining purpose?
cards.back: The Massachusetts Driver Retraining Course addresses driving behavior rather than teaching vehicle-driving skills.

cards.front: What is the rule for retraining information packet?
cards.back: After notice of at least three surchargeable events, the RMV sends a packet explaining retraining, fees and enrollment.

cards.front: What is the rule for retraining format?
cards.back: The driver-retraining program lasts eight hours, usually as two four-hour meetings, with a single Saturday meeting sometimes available.

cards.front: What is the rule for retraining limitations?
cards.back: Completing driver retraining does not erase offenses or surcharges from the driving record and does not replace other required programs.

decks.domain: Civil/criminal violations, crashes, records and retraining

cards.front: What is the rule for parked vehicle collision?
cards.back: Collision with a parked vehicle is one of the listed fault standards, whether that vehicle was lawfully or unlawfully parked.

cards.front: What is the rule for rear end fault standard?
cards.back: A rear-end collision is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for out of lane collision?
cards.back: An out-of-lane collision is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for signal fault standard?
cards.back: Failure to signal is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for traffic control caution?
cards.back: Failure to proceed cautiously from a traffic signal or sign is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for wrong side collision?
cards.back: A collision on the wrong side of the road is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for wrong direction standard?
cards.back: Traveling in the wrong direction is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for uncontrolled intersection?
cards.back: A collision at an uncontrolled intersection is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for backing collision?
cards.back: A collision while backing is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for turn across travel path?
cards.back: A collision during a left turn or U-turn across another vehicle’s travel path is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for entering from roadside?
cards.back: Leaving a parked position, parking lot, alley or driveway is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for open door standard?
cards.back: Opening or having opened a vehicle door is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for single vehicle standard?
cards.back: A single-vehicle collision is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for driving rule standard?
cards.back: Failure to obey driving rules and regulations is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for unattended vehicle?
cards.back: An unattended-vehicle collision is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for merging collision?
cards.back: A collision while merging onto a highway or into a rotary is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for noncontact causation?
cards.back: Causing a collision without physical contact is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for emergency yielding standard?
cards.back: Failing to yield to emergency vehicles when the law requires is one of the listed fault standards.

cards.front: What is the rule for T intersection standard?
cards.back: A collision at a T intersection after entering from the side road is one of the listed fault standards.
